# California LLC fee and franchise tax; foreign qualification

*Citation:* Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code §§17941, 17942, 23153; Cal. Corp. Code §17708.02  
*Status in this library:* in force

Every LLC doing business in California pays the $800 annual tax and a gross-receipts fee ($900 at $250k–$499,999; $2,500 at $500k–$999,999 ...). A Delaware LLC doing business in California must register as a foreign LLC and pays the same amounts; failure bars it from maintaining an action in California courts and incurs penalties.
########## form_2553_deadline.md
# Form 2553 — when to file

*Citation:* IRS Form 2553 Instructions  
*Status in this library:* in force

To be effective for a tax year, file no more than 2 months and 15 days after the beginning of that tax year, or at any time during the preceding year. Late-election relief under Rev. Proc. 2013-30 requires reasonable cause and that all shareholders were eligible for the entire period.
########## irc_1361_excerpt.md
# IRC §1361(b) — small business corporation defined

*Citation:* 26 U.S.C. §1361(b)(1)  
*Status in this library:* in force

(b)(1) In general. — For purposes of this subchapter, the term "small business corporation" means a domestic corporation which is not an ineligible corporation and which does not— (A) have more than 100 shareholders, (B) have as a shareholder a person (other than an estate, a trust described in subsection (c)(2), or an organization described in subsection (c)(6)) who is not an individual, **(C) have a nonresident alien as a shareholder**, and (D) have more than 1 class of stock.

*(§1362(d)(2): an election terminates on the day the corporation ceases to be a small business corporation; the corporation is then a C corporation.)*
########## irc_199a_sstb.md
# IRC §199A — qualified business income; specified service trade or business

*Citation:* 26 U.S.C. §199A(d)(2); (e)(2)  
*Status in this library:* in force

The 20% deduction is not available for a **specified service trade or business** (including **consulting**, health, law, accounting, financial services, and any business where the principal asset is the reputation or skill of its employees) once taxable income exceeds the threshold (2026: approximately $200,300 single / $400,600 joint; verify) plus the phase-in range ($75,000 / $150,000). Below the threshold the SSTB limitation does not apply. W-2 wages paid by an S corporation to its owner are **not** QBI; distributions are. Guaranteed payments from a partnership are not QBI.
########## irc_351_excerpt.md
# IRC §351 — transfer to corporation controlled by transferor

*Citation:* 26 U.S.C. §351(a), (d); §368(c)  
*Status in this library:* in force

(a) No gain or loss shall be recognized if property is transferred to a corporation by one or more persons solely in exchange for stock in such corporation and immediately after the exchange such person or persons are in control (as defined in section 368(c)) of the corporation. **(d) Services ... — For purposes of this section, stock issued for (1) services ... shall not be considered as issued in return for property.** §368(c): control means ownership of at least 80 percent of the total combined voting power and 80 percent of each other class.

*Stock issued for services is compensation income to the recipient at fair market value when substantially vested (§83).*
########## irc_721_and_revproc_93-27.md
# IRC §721 and Rev. Proc. 93-27 — partnership contributions and profits interests

*Citation:* 26 U.S.C. §721; Rev. Proc. 93-27, 1993-2 C.B. 343; Rev. Proc. 2001-43  
*Status in this library:* in force

§721(a): No gain or loss shall be recognized to a partnership or to any of its partners in the case of a contribution of property to the partnership in exchange for an interest in the partnership. (No 80% control requirement.)

Rev. Proc. 93-27 §4.01: if a person receives a **profits interest** for the provision of services to or for the benefit of a partnership in a partner capacity, the IRS will not treat the receipt as a taxable event. A profits interest is one that would give the holder nothing on an immediate liquidation at fair market value. A **capital interest** (a share of existing capital) received for services is taxable compensation at receipt or vesting. Rev. Proc. 2001-43: an unvested profits interest is treated as held from grant if the holder is treated as a partner from grant; a protective §83(b) election within 30 days is customary.
########## irc_7701b_substantial_presence.md
# IRC §7701(b)(3) — substantial presence test

*Citation:* 26 U.S.C. §7701(b)(3)(A)  
*Status in this library:* in force

An individual meets the substantial presence test for a calendar year if (i) the individual was present in the United States on at least 31 days during the calendar year, and (ii) the sum of the number of days present in the current year + **1/3** of the days in the first preceding year + **1/6** of the days in the second preceding year equals or exceeds **183**. An alien who does not hold a green card and does not meet the test is a nonresident alien for the year (absent a first-year election under §7701(b)(4)).
########## irc_83b.md
# IRC §83(b) election

*Citation:* 26 U.S.C. §83(b); Treas. Reg. §1.83-2  
*Status in this library:* in force

A person who performs services in connection with which property is transferred may elect to include in gross income the excess of the fair market value at transfer over the amount paid, **by filing the election not later than 30 days after the date of transfer**. No extension is available. Absent the election, income is recognized as the property vests, at the value at each vesting date.
########## llc_buy_sell_checklist.md
# Operating agreement — buy-sell and governance checklist

*Citation:* Practitioner checklist (ABA Business Law Section, paraphrased)  
*Status in this library:* in force

Trigger events: death, disability, divorce (spousal interest), bankruptcy, voluntary departure, for-cause removal. Price: formula or appraisal; discounts. Payment terms. Vesting of founder units with repurchase at cost for unvested units. Deadlock resolution for 50/50 owners (mediation → buy-sell shotgun). Drag-along/tag-along. Transfer restrictions and spousal consent in community-property jurisdictions.
########## reasonable_compensation.md
# Reasonable compensation for S corporation shareholder-employees

*Citation:* Rev. Rul. 74-44; *Watson v. Commissioner*, 668 F.3d 1008 (8th Cir. 2012); IRS Fact Sheet FS-2008-25  
*Status in this library:* in force

An S corporation shareholder who performs substantial services must be paid reasonable compensation as wages before distributions. In a personal-services business where the shareholders generate essentially all of the revenue, courts have recharacterized distributions as wages where salary was set far below what comparable professionals earn (*Watson*: $24,000 salary vs. ~$200,000 of distributions recharacterized in large part). Payroll taxes, penalties and interest follow.
